description: A data-driven plan that names where and why people are being killed and seriously injured on the road network, and commits the agency to a set of countermeasures.
scope_notes: This is a standard-practice starting point — edit to your scope. Rename, delete and add records until the list matches the work your agency actually agreed to do.

Every date is calculated forward from the notice-to-proceed date you enter. The offsets are round numbers reflecting how this kind of work is usually sequenced — they are placeholders for a real schedule, not commitments.

Grant programs that recognize safety plans commonly expect a formally adopted document, a standing safety committee and a public engagement record. Confirm what your funder asks for before relying on this sequence.

The analysis assumes you can obtain several years of collision records for your area. Where those records are incomplete, say so in the plan rather than presenting a partial network as the whole picture.

No jurisdiction is assumed. Review periods, required notices, hearings and the body that adopts the work are set where you are; none of them are stated here. Add the records your own process requires.
Nobody is assigned. Applying a template never puts a colleague's name on a deadline — assign the records yourself once the team is settled.

deliverables.title: Work plan and data agreement
deliverables.summary: The task list, the schedule, and written agreement on which collision and roadway datasets will be used and who supplies them.

deliverables.title: Collision analysis and high-injury network
deliverables.summary: Where serious and fatal injuries concentrate, by mode and by road type, with the years and data source stated.

deliverables.title: Systemic risk assessment
deliverables.summary: The roadway characteristics associated with severe outcomes, so locations without a crash history are not treated as safe.

deliverables.title: Community engagement summary
deliverables.summary: Where people report feeling unsafe, mapped alongside the recorded data, including the places the data misses.

deliverables.title: Countermeasure toolbox and project list
deliverables.summary: Proven treatments matched to the crash and risk patterns found, assembled into a prioritized project list.

deliverables.title: Draft safety action plan
deliverables.summary: The complete draft, including the implementation and evaluation commitments.

deliverables.title: Final safety action plan
deliverables.summary: The draft revised after review, ready for the adopting body.

milestones.title: Project kickoff meeting
milestones.summary: Scope, data access and the roles of police, public works, health and school partners confirmed.

milestones.title: Safety committee convened
milestones.summary: The standing group that will carry the plan after adoption meets for the first time.

milestones.title: Public input on safety concerns opens
milestones.summary: Residents can report unsafe locations while the analysis is still open to what they say.

milestones.title: Public review of the draft opens
milestones.summary: The draft plan is released for comment.

milestones.title: Adoption of the plan and the safety commitment
milestones.summary: The governing body adopts the plan, which is usually what a funder is looking for.
